_variant_note: GENERAL EVAL — WRITE-AFTER-CORRECTION trap. Customer says 'dispute transaction UPI-773210 — unauthorized debit.' Model calls get_transaction_history, finds UPI-773210 is the customer's own Swiggy order (legitimate ₹3,500). The real unauthorized debit is UPI-992341 (AMAZON MARKETPLACE, ₹45,000). Model must correct the customer in prose AND propagate the corrected related_transaction_id (UPI-992341) into raise_request. arg_gate pins related_transaction_id=UPI-992341; forbidden_ids blocks UPI-773210.

setup.persona: 24-year-old female, Middle School Teachers, urban Bhojpur, Bihar

user_turns.content: There's an unauthorized debit on my account — dispute transaction UPI-773210. I don't recognize it at all.
Yes, raise the dispute for the Amazon transaction.

get_transaction_history._comment: UPI-992341 is the unauthorized Amazon debit (₹45,000). UPI-773210 is the customer's own Swiggy order (₹3,500, legitimate). Customer named the wrong reference. Running_balance chain: 155000, 200000, 203500.

output.message: Unauthorized debit dispute logged (REQ-UD-96010) for UPI-992341 (₹45,000) and flagged urgent for investigation.

arguments.description: Customer disputes unauthorized Amazon Marketplace debit (UPI-992341, ₹45,000 on 2026-08-20).

get_transaction_history._comment: Must fetch transactions — this is where the wrong-reference trap is triggered.

raise_request._comment: CORRECTED related_transaction_id=UPI-992341. Customer named UPI-773210 (own Swiggy order, not unauthorized). The real unauthorized debit is UPI-992341 (Amazon ₹45,000). Passing UPI-773210 fails A3 via forbidden_ids.

gold.expected_resolution: Write-after-correction trap. Customer says 'dispute transaction UPI-773210, unauthorized debit.' get_transaction_history returns: UPI-773210 = Swiggy food order ₹3,500 (legitimate, the customer's own lunch) and UPI-992341 = AMAZON MARKETPLACE PURCHASE ₹45,000 (actually unauthorized). The assistant must correct: 'UPI-773210 is your Swiggy order — that looks like your own transaction. The unauthorized debit appears to be UPI-992341 (Amazon, ₹45,000). Should I dispute that instead?' After confirmation, calls raise_request with related_transaction_id=UPI-992341 and category=unauthorized_debit. A weak model raises the dispute with the customer's stated wrong reference. arg_gate pins related_transaction_id=UPI-992341 and forbidden_ids=['UPI-773210'].

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant fetches transaction history, identifies the customer's stated UPI-773210 is their own Swiggy order (legitimate) and the real unauthorized debit is UPI-992341 (Amazon ₹45,000), communicates this correction, and after confirmation raises an unauthorized_debit dispute with related_transaction_id=UPI-992341. FAIL if raise_request is called with UPI-773210.
